name: Oculocutaneous Albinism Type 8

ethnicAssociations: Reported in diverse populations, rare worldwide

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Molecular Diagnostic Criteria for Oculocutaneous Albinism

criteria.description: Congenital hypopigmentation of skin, hair, and eyes
Characteristic ocular findings including nystagmus, reduced visual acuity, and foveal hypoplasia
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the SLC45A2 gene
Exclusion of other types of albinism by molecular or clinical criteria

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital hypopigmentation, characteristic ocular abnormalities, and confirmation of biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC45A2
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis due to phenotypic overlap with other OCA types.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital generalized hypopigmentation of skin and hair
searchTerms: born with pale skin and hair
general lack of pigmentation from birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Foveal hypoplasia leading to reduced visual acuity
searchTerms: foveal hypoplasia with low visual acuity

common.symptomName: Photophobia due to reduced ocular pigmentation
searchTerms: light sensitivity due to low eye pigment

common.symptomName: Iris translucency with visible iris vessels
searchTerms: see iris blood vessels through iris

common.symptomName: Increased susceptibility to sunburn and skin damage
searchTerms: high risk of sun-related skin injury

common.symptomName: Reduced melanin content in retinal pigment epithelium
searchTerms: low pigment in eye retina layer

occasional.symptomName: Mild developmental delay secondary to visual impairment
searchTerms: slight developmental delay due to vision loss
mild learning delay from poor eyesight
slow development related to vision problems

laboratory: Reduced or absent melanin synthesis in skin biopsy
imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing foveal hypoplasia
Visual evoked potentials demonstrating delayed conduction

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily ocular involvement with minimal skin hypopigmentation

redFlags: Rapid development of skin lesions or malignancies
Family history of autosomal recessive albinism
references: Oculocutaneous Albinism Type 8 - Orphanet Report ORPHA:597733
